summary: Iter 100 — Tested Mira lead intent scoring + rescore API, password policy on signup/reset, CRM bulk-delete API (tenant-scoped), and frontend flows for SignupSalon PasswordStrength, ResetPassword, SuccessStories, Customers bulk-delete, and HQ MiraLeadAgent cards. 6/7 pytest tests PASS; one FAIL is a Pydantic-vs-policy ordering issue on /api/auth/reset-password (details below). All frontend selectors from spec render correctly.

minor.issue: ResetIn.new_password has Pydantic Field(..., min_length=8), so a <8-char payload (spec example 'weak') returns 422 Unprocessable Entity BEFORE the password_policy_errors() check runs — spec expects 400 'Password needs …'. Passwords ≥8 chars that still violate the policy (e.g. 'weakpassword') correctly return 400 'Password needs an uppercase letter, a number, a symbol'. Fix: drop min_length=8 from ResetIn so the policy branch always owns the error contract (as /public/signup-salon already does — SalonSignupIn.password also has min_length=8 but that path happens to accept 'weakpassword' which is ≥8). Low-impact — frontend already blocks submit on weak passwords, but violates the documented API contract.

ui_bugs.issue: After ticking crm-select-all → bulk-delete-customers-btn appears with correct text 'Delete selected (20)'. However clicking crm-select-all a second time to untick leaves the button still visible (bulk btn count still truthy). Spec says 'Untick → button disappears'. Likely cause: the header checkbox is tri-state or the second click re-selects. Needs verification in Customers.jsx removeSelected / selection state effect.

Clicking bulk-delete-customers-btn did NOT fire a window.confirm dialog in headless test — may be an inline modal (not window.confirm) or require different trigger. Spec says 'confirm dialog appears'. Please verify it is a native confirm() or a shadcn Dialog with data-testid.

rca of the issue: Reset-password 422-vs-400: Pydantic validates body before the FastAPI handler body executes, so min_length=8 on new_password short-circuits with 422 before the password_policy_errors() check inside the handler ever runs. Simplest fix: change `new_password: str = Field(..., min_length=8, max_length=128)` to `new_password: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128)` (keep max for abuse), then the handler emits the uniform 400 'Password needs …' message.
